prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Summary of 2001 manifesto proposals (ideological framing and names omitted)

- Family and education
  - Targeted tax cuts: higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; transferable allowance for couples with young children or caring responsibilities; remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; reform in‑work credit to be paid to the caring parent.
  - School autonomy (“Free Schools”): heads/governors control staffing, pay, admissions via home–school agreements; easier exclusion for disruptive pupils with off-site Progress Centres; successful schools free to expand; new schools allowed from faith, parent, charitable and company providers; parents can trigger special inspections and management change; redirect bureaucracy savings directly to schools.
  - Students and universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20,000; no top‑up fees; create university endowments.

- Crime and justice
  - Increase police numbers; cut bureaucracy; visible policing (e.g., paperwork done on the beat); parish constables; focus on antisocial behaviour.
  - Expand secure training places for persistent young offenders; link release to behaviour/qualifications.
  - Mandatory prison for selling drugs to under‑16s; tougher sentences near schools.
  - End automatic early release; require prison work with proceeds to victims/families.
  - Lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protect children online.
  - Stronger victim rights: named contacts in police/CPS; written reasons if charges dropped; update self‑defence and double jeopardy rules.

- Economy and regulation
  - Tax reductions funded by £8bn in savings (excluding schools/NHS/police/defence): abolish taxes on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; married couple’s allowance; higher Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; business rates cuts; abolish IR35; targeted regeneration breaks; relief for approved share options.
  - Simpler, more transparent tax/accounts; Capital Gains Tax simplification with lower rates.
  - Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; small-firm exemptions; focus utility regulators on competition.
  - Replace Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear’s role.
  - Keep the pound; bolster monetary policy independence; external fiscal scrutiny.

- Health
  - Match planned NHS funding but shift control to clinicians; Patient’s Guarantee of maximum waits based on clinical need with right to alternative NHS/private provision; more choice for patients/GPs; empower ward sisters/matrons; expand practice nurse roles; specialist surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund; increase hospice funding; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

- Older people and care
  - Raise basic state pension (larger uplift for over‑75s); option to consolidate certain payments into a higher tax‑free pension; increase age allowance by £2,000 to remove ~1m from income tax; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; explore funded pension option for younger workers; protect assets for those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

- International and defence
  - In the EU but retain veto; keep the pound; seek treaty flexibility/reserved powers; strengthen the single market and anti‑fraud measures.
  - Prioritise NATO; oppose separate EU military structures; maintain independent deterrent; support missile defence; reach full manning; reserves reform; exempt armed forces from certain human rights constraints as other states do.
  - Aid: work toward 0.7% GNP; double share via charities; improve EU aid or permit bilateral alternatives; push debt relief, HIV/AIDS, conflict resolution; envoy for religious freedom.
  - Trade: pursue EU‑NAFTA free trade area toward global free trade by 2020; align diplomacy and trade promotion.

- Asylum
  - House new applicants in secure reception centres pending decisions; presume refusal for safe‑country claims; create a removals agency for rejected cases.

- Welfare and civil society
  - Office of Civil Society; eliminate irrecoverable VAT for charities.
  - Replace existing job schemes with outcome‑based contracts paying for sustained employment; “can work, must work” principle; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
  - Improve disabled savings rules; new Incapacity Benefit agency funding rehabilitation; national anti‑fraud squad; clean up National Insurance numbers.

- Town, country, transport, environment
  - Foot‑and‑mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP with more national/local control; honest food labelling; reduce rural red tape; cut business rates for key rural services; benefit card to sustain post offices; support rural transport.
  - Abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; more local control; protect green/“blue belt” areas; rural affairs select committee.
  - Urban regeneration companies with powers over policing, schools, planning, and housing renewal; promote brownfield building; expand homeownership (right‑to‑buy, rent‑to‑mortgage, homesteading).
  - Transport: long‑term plans; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe with strict enforcement; charge foreign lorries; revive rail; cut fuel duty; promote cleaner fuels/vehicles.
  - Environment: emissions trading, conservation, renewables, cleaner generation.

- Culture, media, sport
  - Privatise Channel 4; £3bn endowment for cultural bodies; simplify lottery rules; strengthen tourism promotion.
  - Protect school sport time/playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; streamline funding.
  - Single media/communications regulator; modernise ownership rules; independent BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

- Democracy and governance
  - Devolve powers to high‑performing “free councils”; fewer central targets; local referendums on large council tax rises.
  - Abolish regional agencies/assemblies; return development powers locally.
  - English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords with independent appointments and elected element; enhance Commons scrutiny (more frequent PM accountability, stronger select committees); retain current general election voting system.
  - Reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and political advisers.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Labour', 'Conservative', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Scottish National Party', 'UK Independence Party']
}
